claims.claim: Reviewers note that vehicles become obsolete and useless shortly after starting because the super speed and gliding traversal mechanics make cars redundant.

citations.review_text:
From the perspective of someone playing the Saints Row series for the first time (co-op): This one didn't hit the right spots for me to shrug off crashing/disconnecting every 10 minutes like the others. Not big into the whole super powers thing, not that it matters as 50% of missions switch them off because they're too strong. This game has the best driving mechanics out of the whole series but cars are rendered completely useless after the first 30 mins. No change in vibe throughout the game like you got with the gangs in 2 and 3, it's just all future tech which is what I liked least about the previous games.

The story is really good though. I liked the game better as it went on.

[h1][b] TLDR: Superpowers make traversal an absolute blast, but clunky combat, a sea of bugs, and wild inconsistency ensure every high point comes bundled with an equally frustrating low.
[/b] [/h1]

[h1]PROS: [/h1]
➕Humor and pop culture references
➕superpowers are fun
➕Main missions offer some creative alternative gameplay elements, i.e side-scrolling beat’em ups

[h1]CONS: [/h1]
➖Less character creation options than SR3
➖Animations are clunky, especially with all the agility that super powers give you
➖So many bugs
➖Story is just mid, and oftentimes nonsensical

My reviews for past Saints games:
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/Synikx/recommended/9480?snr=1_5_9__402]Saint’s Row 2 (SR2)[/url]
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/Synikx/recommended/978300?snr=1_5_9__402]Saint’s Row 3 Remastered (SR3)[/url]

[h1] [b] Content (Game world/Narrative) – [5/10] [/b] [/h1]
The game world takes place between a simulated world of Steelport and the real world of alien ships, but really, most of the better open world gameplay occurs in the simulated world. The map is fairly large and full of things to do. 

The narrative, like previous SR games, is wacky, crude, crazy, and often full of plot holes. It’s definitely something you shouldn’t take seriously. I mean literally the first 10 minutes of the game has you saving the country from a nuclear missile while Aerosmith is playing, then planet Earth is invaded by aliens and blown up. Literally the opening part of the game!
From a complete story viewpoint, I found the narrative mediocre. Like many parts of the game, it has excellent parts, and terrible parts. 

[h1][b] Gameplay (Mechanics/Difficulty) – [5/10] [/b] [/h1]
The gameplay loop doesn’t change a whole lot from SR3 - you pretty much do missions, get money, spend money on abilities or gun. Here though, superpowers adds a very nice touch. The super sprint and jump means that you’ll never want to ride a car. Add in the glide and traversal is a blast. Speaking of, there’s a b…

It's more a novelty you coop with someone for a couple of days. There's some fun but it's really a temporary thing. The mechanics are just kinda bad. You and a fried can have a laugh and quickly get the most outta the game in a few hours, but just as you start to get the hang of the controls and mechanics, you realize they are kinda poorly done. The running the jumping the gliding the fighting the guns, they all kinda feel crappy. Fov is and camera is kinda a problem, about the only thing that's fun mechanically is the running attacks triggering some kinda complex takedown. It shouldn't be more fun, as standard as it is, driving a car, than it is running and gliding. It's just there is better games at this point, I would say skip it now and play something else.

claims.claim: The open-world map reuses locations and side activities from Saints Row: The Third.

citations.review_text:
Saints Row IV takes the exact map from Saints Row: The Third but replaces gang wars with an alien invasion and superpowers. It abandons all realism to become a sci-fi comedy sandbox. Which I did enjoy. With the older games you never knew what you were going to get. 

This game gets some flack for reusing the map. But I like it, since I know where everything is already and I'm familiar with Steelport. I know people don't like the recycled open world side activities which mask themselves as campaign missions. I didn't personally mind it this time around. But what really bugs me is that it still suffers from performance issues. Like sound bugs, frame drops, and crashes. Though I didn't experience any crashes my buddy did. 

I also hate that I have to connect to the Epic games bs. 

This game is still worth playing in the big TWO SIX.

[b] P. S. If you have difficulties in the walktrough, this guide will be very useful: [/b]

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3561496240

[h1] Stop bugging the boss, Shaundi, and Pierce [/h1]

The game feels less like a full-fledged sequel and more like an extended, wonky DLC for the third installment — same locations, same side quests, slightly different scenery, and a couple of new mechanics.  

The story is a mix of disconnected clichés: first terrorism, then an alien invasion, then a Matrix-style simulation. It all comes across as a mess, and the game can’t decide what it wants to be — a superhero action flick, a standalone comedy, or just an empty open world. In the end, it ends up as a weird hodgepodge of parodies of other titles with no real backbone or Saints Row spirit.  

There are far more gameplay problems than new features. Superpowers are handed out without any setup or character development along the story, and they don’t make up for the overall repetitiveness: many mechanics and the damage balance are just as weird and off as in previous entries. The feeling of “they just repackaged the old stuff” never really goes away.

The Russian localization is sloppy. Lots of mistakes, mixed-up pronouns, wrong name translations (and sometimes no translation at all).

If you didn't like Saints Row 3, there's no clear reason to get the fourth one. It's an awkward collection of ideas, fan service, and an attempt to push nostalgia from previous games in the series, which probably won't even please SR fans.

[h3] Verdict: [/h3] https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3612049014

[i] P. S. 2x. Did you like the review or my profile? Drop a Steam reward for the review. Thanks to your support, I don't lose the point of playing and writing reviews! [/i]

Saints Row IV should have been a DLC for the third game rather than a standalone sequel. While I have a nostalgic soft spot for the soundtrack and the dubstep guns that I absolutely loved as a kid, the rest of the experience falls flat. The introduction of superhero powers completely ruins the game's balance, making vehicles and customization pointless, while the recycled map feels lazy and uninspired. It’s a repetitive, identity-clashing mess that lacks the charm of the earlier entries, proving that a great playlist can't save a game that should have stayed an expansion.

+ The zaniness is great, the powers, the loyalty missions, the weapoins, the side gigs etc there are a LOT of them. 
+ ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ those collectable orbs... Crackdown type addiction to getting distracted by those and just flying around listening to music and getting them
- It doesn't go as hard or land as hilariously as SR3. The music drops, the gratuity, etc. And I bought the non "low violence version" through keys to get around dumb Aussie censorship.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that co-op sessions suffer from disconnections, desyncs, and mission progress bugs.

citations.review_text:
I really love this game but the crashes are so annoying, if you have a console it's better to get it on it rather than on PC.

Edit: and if you are playing this in coop, this game is filled with desync that causes disconnections and replaying the mission again everytime that happens.

Edit 2: I just finished the game and the DLC missions yesterday and it seems like if you are playing in coop as well there will be progression bug in map where despite you have collected all collectibles and done all targets there will be still missing numbers on your end and there's no solution to this, some achievements will also not unlock despite meeting the requirements for them and the only way to do so is to unlock them through Steam achievement manager.

As a person who 100% completed this game, I can confidently say that this is by far the worst saints row game in the series in terms of being able to even play the game.
Pros:
-The powers are very fun to use
-The side content is an improvement from saints row the third
-The story missions had some cool stuff like the tank section

Cons:
-The game crashes very often
-Playing coop is pure chaos with constant disconnects
-Missions soft locked in coop due to random crashes strictly for coop
-Progression in coop is super bugged always reseting Progress 
-Challanges/achievements progression crashes making some borderline imposibile
-Npc vanshing or getting stuck
-Having to restart steam to be able to progress through a mission... which then disconnects my coop partner and having to do the whole reset again

Overall the negatives heavily outweigh the positives, so the grade for the game is sadly a 4/10 for ruining the coop experience that is the only thing making this game fun.
